notes: yēš is what makes the clause possessive and takes 'thou hast' with its supplied pronoun, on the pattern rule 43 gives for a morpheme that carries the possession by itself; the head stays on 'hast', since the existential's own sense is the possession and not the pronoun.
'anything to say' is the noun's own recasting under rules 46 and 31, headed on the English verb carrying millîn's lexeme; the competing head 'anything' is named in the unit note.
The bare infinitive construct has no preposition before it, so the English infinitive marker belongs to the infinitive's unit (rule 52's closing sentence).
